Same-isolate gene/phenotype co-occurrence, not proof that CMLA6 alone caused resistance. The paper names CMLA6 and reports the native isolate phenotype as data not shown; no zone diameter or clinical breakpoint interpretation is inferred. Its beta-lactam experiments in other hosts are not chloramphenicol evidence for this isolate. UniProtKB:Q933G9 is retained as reference context only: it combines CmlA6 and cmlA1 annotations from separate source contexts. The source-reported deposit AF294653.1 is not a genome assembly. No exact experimental protein, allele, strain TaxID or genome is assigned. Compound scope follows named chloramphenicol; the tested preparation was not independently re-identified.

The comparison concerns laboratory derivatives of the TK24 background, not native-donor susceptibility or species-wide resistance. NCBITaxon:457428 denotes the TK24 background, not the experimental derivative. The reported donor is Streptomyces rishiriensis DSM 40489. UniProtKB:Q83WB8 is reference-only (entry version 120, sequence version 2); the archive succession does not establish the exact experimental allele. The 2003 study leaves ParY enzymatic function unresolved. No induced point mutant, clinical category, numerical AST, derivative TaxID or experimental genome is assigned. Compound scope follows the source's named structure in Figure 1A, not independent re-identification of the tested preparation.

The tested subjects are TM300-derived laboratory strains, not the unmodified background. Staphylococcus epidermidis Tue3298 is the donor. The three-component result does not establish individual sufficiency; transport remains a hypothesis. No derivative TaxID, genome, numerical AST or clinical category is assigned.

The primary paper reports a functional result in a heterologous host derived from S. albus J1074, explicitly with data not shown. The proposed resistant threonyl-tRNA synthetase route is not directly demonstrated in this report, so mechanism_type remains UNKNOWN. Native donor Streptomyces parvulus Tu4055 is not the tested host. Donor reference UniProtKB:Q70HZ0 (EMBL:AJ580915 / CAE45679.1; entry version 112, sequence version 1) and NCBITaxon:146923 identify source/reference context, not the exact experimental allele. NCBITaxon:1888 is a species-name reference for S. albus; the J1074 taxonomy search returned multiple candidates, and no strain identifier was selected. Background, donor and derivative are not interchangeable. No exact allele, protein accession, strain TaxID, genome, quantitative AST or clinical category is assigned.

raw_value: The crystal structure of two of these members shows that this domain has a ferredoxin like fold and is likely to exists as at least homodimers. Sulphate ions are are located at the dimer interfaces, which are thought to confer additional stability. Although the function of this domain remains to be identified, its structure suggests a role in protein-protein interactions possibly regulated by the binding of small-molecule ligands [[cite:PUB00019479]]. Solution of the structure of the hyperthermophilic anaerobic Thermotoga maritima sequence, UniProtKB:Q9WYV6, shows that this has a beta-alpha-beta-beta-alpha-beta ferredoxin-like fold and assembles as a homotetramer. It was possible to identify a pocket in each monmer that bound an unidentified ligand. It was also found that it bound charged thiamine though not hydroxymethyl pyrimidine. It is proposed that it is transporting charged thiamine around the cytoplasm. Under oxidative conditions this bacterium is under stress, and the transcriiptional unit within which this protein is expressed is up-regulated in these conditions, suggesting that the chelation of cytoplasmic thaimine is part of the response mechanism to such oxidatvie stress, which is mediated by this family [[cite:PUB00055842]].

The SRAP family functions as a DNA-associated autoproteolytic switch that recruits diverse repair enzymes onto DNA damage. We propose that the human protein Q96FZ2:UniProtKB, the eukaryotic member of the SRAP family, which has been recently shown to bind specifically to DNA with 5-hydroxymethylcytosine, 5-formylcytosine and 5-carboxycytosine, is a sensor for these oxidized bases generated by the TET (tetrahedral aminopeptidase of the M42 family) enzymes from methylcytosine. Hence, its autoproteolytic activity might help it act as a switch that recruits DNA repair enzymes to remove these oxidized methylcytosine species as part of the DNA demethylation pathway downstream of the TET enzymes.

YcaO is an ATP- an Mg2+-binding protein involved in the peptidic biosynthesis of azoline. There three motifs involved in the binding are, in UniProtKB:P75838, 71-79: Sx3ExxER, 184-203: Sx6Ex3Qx3ExxER, and 286-290: RxxxE. Three slightly different functional families are represented in this family, proteins involved in TOMM (thiazole/oxazole-modified microcin) biogenesis, non-TOMM proteins such as UniProtKB:P75838, and TfuA-associated non-TOMM proteins involved in trifolitoxin biosynthesis. UniProtKB:P75838 hydrolyses ATP to AMP and pyrophosphate [[cite:PUB00078765]].

Two structures have been solved for members of this large (>500 members) family of bacterial proteins present mostly in environmental bacteria and metagenomes (distant homologues are also present in several Plasmodium species). TOPSAN analysis for pdb:3pjy shows that there is much similarity with the other solved structure, pdb:3m7a, solved for UniProt:Q2GA55 (Saro_0823), a homologue of Thermotoga maritima TM1668, UniProt:Q9X1Z6., The homologue in Caulobacter crescentus (CC1388), UniProt:Q9A8G6, is associated with CspD, a cold shock protein (CC1387), UniProt:Q9A8G7. However, the genomic context of UniProt:Q2GA55 is most conserved with a putative xylose isomerase, suggesting a possible role in extracellular sugar processing. Saro_0821, UniProt:Q2GA57, is annotated as an AMP-dependent synthetase and ligase. PDB:3m7a structure corresponds to the C-terminal (27-165) fragment of the YP_496102 (Saro_0823) protein and it is structurally unique, as the best hits from Dali have a Z-score of 3.8 (1nt0, 2j1t, 3kq4) and it is thus a likely candidate for a new fold. Interestingly, many of the top Dali hits are involved in sugar metabolism. There are no obvious active site-like cavities on the protein surface of 3m7a (http://www.topsan.org/Proteins/JCSG/).

The catalytic triad of this esterase enzyme comprises residues Ser127, His403 and Asp391 in UniProtKB:P70665 [[cite:PUB00039360],[cite:PUB00078761]].

This is a family of trypsin-6-like proteins found in nematodes that are part of the chymotrypsin family S1, ie a serine peptidase. The C. elegans sequence UniProt:O01566 is trypsin-6: all the active site residues are present (His90, Asp168, Ser267).

The alkaline shock protein Asp23 was identified as an alkaline shock protein that was expressed in a sigmaB-dependent manner in Staphylococcus aureus [[cite:PUB00008427]]. Following an alkaline shock Asp23 accumulates in the soluble protein fraction of the S. aureus cell. Asp23 is one of the most abundant proteins in the cytosolic protein fraction of stationary S. aureus cells, with a copy-number of >25000 per cell. A second Asp23-family protein, AmaP, which is encoded within the asp23-operon, is required to localise Asp23 to the cell membrane [[cite:PUB00075359]]. The overall function for the family is thus a cell envelope-related one in Gram-positive bacteria. UniProtKB:Q2FW64 [[cite:PUB00075359]].

This is a family of putative bacterial lipoproteins necessary for the uptake of haem-iron. The structure of UniProtKB:Q0PBW2, PDB:2g5g, comprises a large parallel beta-sheet with flanking alpha-helices and a smaller domain consisting of alpha-helices. Two cofacial haem groups (~3.5 Angstom apart with an inter-iron distance of 4.4 Angstrom) bind in a pocket formed by a dimer of two ChaN monomers [[cite:PUB00075535],[cite:PUB00040938]].

This family of uncharacterised integral membrane proteins appears to be restricted to proteobacteria. These proteins are related to the DoxX family [pfam:PF07681]. Members of this family form a confident homodimeric structure, for example UniProtKB:A0A4R5FQM0 iPTM=0.94.

Archaeal protein of unknown function. A fungal member UniProtKB:M2LN89 is clearly a Flavine-reductase enzyme by homology, and UniProtKB:O28442 has been shown to bind riboflavin 5'-phosphate (unpublished structural Xray analysis).

Amidase_YiiX is a family of permuted papain-like amidases. It has amidase specificity for the amide bond between a lipid and an amino acid (or peptide). From the structure, a tetramer, each monomer is made up of a layered alpha-beta fold with a central, 6-stranded, antiparallel beta-sheet that is protected by helices on either side. The catalytic Cys154 in UniProtKB:Q74NK7, PDB:3kw0, is located on the N-terminus of helix alphaF. The two additional helices located above Cys154 contribute to the formation of the active site, where the lysine ligand is bound [[cite:PUB00075488]].

This family represents a short region in the middle of largely plant proteins that belong to the TCDB:1.A.1.23.2 family of the voltage-gated ion channel superfamily, eg UniProtKB:Q5H8A6, Q5H8A5 and Q4VY51.

CmpB is a family of membrane proteins that are likely to be part of a two-component type IV ABC-transporter system. Families can transport multiple drugs including ethidium and fluoroquinolones. UniProtKB:Q83XH0 is a member of TCDB family 3.A.1.121.4.

SPP is a family of signal-peptide aspartyl proteases. The family carries the characteristic catalytic aspartate GXGD motif, and members are integral membrane peptidases of the presenilin-type with nine transmembrane regions. UniProtKB:Q18K19 is part of the TCDB family 1.A.54.3.4, the presenilin er Ca(2+) leak channel (presenilin).

AlaE is a family of Gram-negative amino-acid transporters. It is not entirely clear why bacteria export metabolites but recent studies have shown that many excrete alanine. AlaE is likely to be the exporter protein for L-alanine. UniProtKB:A8ANM6, UniProt:G4R961 and UniProt:H5SVY7 are classified as putative alanine exporters [[cite:PUB00060685]].

ThrE is a family of bacterial and Archaeal proteins that catalyse the export of L-threonine from the cell [[cite:PUB00075540]]. UniProtKB:Q79VD1 has been characterised as being necessary for this export. The domain exhibits 10 putative TMs and catalyses the proton-motive-force-dependent efflux of threonine and serine [[cite:PUB00075541]].

This family consists of several hypothetical bacterial proteins of around 440 residues in length. The function of this family is unknown. Many members carry 11 or 12 transmembrane regions, suggesting that they might be transporters. One family member, UniProtKB:Q821X2 is classified by TCDB as being an NhaE type of Na+/H+ antiporter.

This is a family of bacterial and archaeal PINc domains. PIN domains are characterised by the conservation of three acidic residues, possibly four, an Asp at residue 13, a Glu at 63, and then Asps at 172 and 194 in UniProtKB:Q58360. Family members include Homologs of Aquifex RNase P (HARP) proteins [[cite:PUB00091006]].

The structure of UniProt:Q5LIB7 has an alpha/alpha toroid fold and is similar structurally to a number of glucoamylases. Most of these structural homologues are glucoamylases, involved in breaking down complex sugars (e.g. starch). The biologically relevant state is likely to be monomeric. The putative active site is located at the centre of the toroid with a well defined large cavity.

ParD-like antitoxin is a family of archaeal and bacterial proteins of a type II bacterial toxin-antitoxin system. Many of the cognate toxins for these molecules fall into family ParE-like_toxin, [pfam:PF15781]. Gene-pairs are expressed from the same operon, the toxin of the pair being expressed first, eg, for UniProtKB:Q3AQ93 and UniProtKB:Q3AQ94.

QSregVF_b is a family of short Pseudomonas proteins that are potential virulence factors. The structure of UniProtKB:Q9HY15 a secreted protein has been solved and deposited as PDB:3npd, from [pfam:PF13652]. It is predicted that these two adjacent proteins form a single transcriptional unit based on the prediction that together they interact with their adjacent protein PotD, which is the putrescine-binding periplasmic protein in the polyamine uptake system comprising PotABCD. These two adjacent proteins are predicted to be quroum-sensing-regulated virulence factors [[cite:PUB00075641]].

This is a family of short ~14 kDa proteins from Psuedomonas. The structure of UniProtKB:Q9HY15 a secreted protein has been solved and deposited as PDB:3npd. It comprises one structural domain with five beta-strands and five alpha-helices. Various comparative structural prediction methods plus its genomic location point to the protein forming a functional dimer with its adjacent genomic partner, UniProtKB:Q9HY14, in [pfam:PF12843]. Together these might be regulated by the other product from the PotABCD operon, namely the putrescine-binding periplasmic protein UniProtKB:Q9HY16. which has been implicated in quorum-sensing. QSregVF is certainly up-regulated in quorum-sensing, and is predicted to be a virulence factor [[cite:PUB00075641]].

TTRAP is a family of small bacterial proteins largely from Clostrium difficile. From comparative and other structural studies of the PDB:2L7K, UniProtKB:Q18AW3, it has been suggested that this family is required for interacting with other proteins in order to facilitate the transfer of the transposon CTn4 between different bacterial species. PDB:2L7K comprises an alpha-helical fold of four alpha-helices leading to the production of two clefts, the larger of which displays two highly conserved residues in close proximity, Glu-8 and Lys-48. The gene concerned is part of an operon within transposon CTn4, and is expressed alongside a putative DNA primase, a DNA topoisomerase and conjugal transfer proteins [[cite:PUB00075684]].

This family of proteins is functionally uncharacterised. This family of proteins is found in bacteria. Proteins in this family are typically between 137 and 164 amino acids in length. These proteins are integral membrane proteins with four transmembrane helices. The contain several conserved histidines and AlphaFold 3 predicts a confident zinc binding site. Structure prediction also suggests that these proteins might form a homotetrameric complex UniProt:A0A3B9LPY9 iPTM=0.9. The four subunits are alternating in different orientations in the presumed membrane. The structure prediction also suggests a central pore between the subunits.

Although this family has overlaps with SLBB, the majority of its sequences are unique. Several family members, eg UniProtKB:A0RGA8, that do not overlap have an LPXTG-cell wall anchor at their C-terminus, a SSF_Family 10_polysaccharide_lyase or Glycosyltransferase structure associated with them in the middle region, as shown by InterPro, as well as this domain at the N-terminus.

This entry represents the VPS13 adaptor binding (VAB) domain, previously known as SHR-BD, found in vacuolar protein sorting-associated protein 13 (VPS13) [[cite:PUB00100501]]. Proteins containing this domain are involved in vesicle fusion, autophagy, and actin regulation [[cite:PUB00100501]] and, through membrane-specific adaptor proteins such as Ypt35, Spo71 and the mitochondrial membrane protein Mcp1, VPS13 proteins are recruited to different membranes. This domain interacts with Ypt35 which recruits VPS13 to endosomal and vacuolar membranes, and with Mcp1 to target VPS13 at mitochondria. Defects in the human protein VPS13A cause chorea-acanthocytosis, an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder [[cite:PUB00100501],[cite:PUB00016718]]. In plants, this domain is found to be the region which interacts with SHR or the SHORT-ROOT transcription factor, a regulator of root-growth and asymmetric cell division that separates ground tissue into endodermis and cortex. The plant protein containing the SHR-BD is named SHRUBBY or SHBY UniProt:Q9FT44 [[cite:PUB00100502]].

This entry represents a domain from a family of uncharacterised proteins in archaea. The proteins in this family are predominantly found in halophilic archaea, particularly within the Halobacteria class. The proteins are generally short, with lengths ranging from 89 to 123 amino acids. The reviewed protein from Halogeometricum borinquense (UniProtKB:E4NSC8) is included in this family.

This ATP-dependent two-event bypass converts sedoheptulose7-phosphate (S7P) through sedoheptulose1, 7-bisphosphate (SBP) to erythrose4-phosphate (E4P) and glycerone phosphate (DHAP). Exact Rhea chemistry is S7P + ATP -> SBP + ADP + H(+), followed by SBP -> E4P + DHAP. Native RXN0-6541 and SEDOBISALDOL-RXN map to directional RHEA31444 and cleavage30169; native 30170 is bidirectional and 30168 is condensation. The generic S7P class is distinct from alpha-pyranose CPD-19339/CHEBI133984. PfkA is a native homotetramer and FbaA a homodimer, not the mixed PfkA/PfkB assembly suggested by the frozen PathBank component list. Reference P0A796/b3916 and P0AB71/b2925 and MG1655 GeneIDs948412/947415 anchor identity; off-taxon GeneIDs93777982/93779073 belong to Shigella sonnei and are rejected. Database taxonomic range and reference identity do not establish unmodified wild-type flux in every strain. PMID19756045 studies BW25113 talA:tet/talB:Cm derivatives, not a sequenced MG1655 assay strain. The double deletion grows on xylose (doubling time110 min versus 100 min wild type); additional pfkA deletion abolishes this growth. deoBC, fbp and tpiA comparisons distinguish alternative routes, with the paper's data-not-shown limitations retained. Growth screening, metabolomics and enzyme assays have distinct media/carbon concentrations. Cultures were at 37 °C, generally in MOPS medium; a common universal medium is not inferred. [PMID:19756045]

The 2009 direct assay uses six-His ASKA PfkA/FbaA, 2 µM enzyme, 5 mM S7P or F6P, 2 mM ATP and 50 mM potassium MOPS at 37 °C for 1 h (five samples). TableIII separates no-enzyme S7P 5.13±0.26 mM with products not detected; PfkA-only S7P 2.91±0.15/SBP 1.15±0.13; both enzymes S7P 3.05±0.14/SBP 0.79±0.11/DHAP0.23±0.02/E4P0.39±0.03; FbaA-only S7P 5.27±0.17 with products not detected; and the F6P comparison yielding FBP/DHAP with E4P not determined. No authentic SBP standard was available: migration reasoning and F1, 6BP calibration were used. Results report m/z369.0 and Methods367.0, an unresolved internal discrepancy rather than a silently corrected observation. [PMID:19756045]

The 2009 original supplementary workbooks retain S7P accumulation of about 45.67-fold on xylose and 101.63-fold on gluconate for the selected mutant/wild-type columns. The description of no notable transcriptional change differs from literal equality: fbaA ratio 1.18 and pfkA1.241 are retained. Isotopomer model fits support the bypass in tested talAB cells; with uptake normalized100, wild-type best-fit bypass values are small nonzero0.004/0.005 and the mutant both-pathway fit is about 29.923/29.181. These are model-specific relative fluxes. Some supplementary MFA equations label the SBP-cleavage product GAP/G3P rather than DHAP; direct products and Rhea define the chemistry, and no TPI event is added to repair a source model. [PMID:19756045]

Supplementary Figure 8 of PMID19756045 uses the Lactococcus lactis pfk ORF in pTRC99A under a trc promoter to complement the E. coli talAB pfkA triple-mutant xylose phenotype (MOPS, 0.2% xylose, 1 mM IPTG). The donor strain/accession is not supplied. This is heterologous complementation, not native L. lactis complete-pathway flux or a reference-protein sequence assignment. [PMID:19756045]

PMID31871051 reconstructs BW25113 talAB and measures xylose growth at 0.33±0.01 h−1 versus wild type 0.39±0.01 in M9; glucose values are0.52 versus 0.49 h−1. Its knockout Methods inconsistently mention pKD3 and pKD4. Orbitrap identification at 368.99 [M-H]− with 199/271 fragments uses mutant extract as a control, not an authentic commercial SBP standard. SBP stability limits, a blank368.804 peak and trace wild-type xylose SBP remain explicit; metabolite detection does not measure wild-type bypass flux. Its PfkA BW25113_3916 in pET-28b(+), DH5α cloning, Rosetta expression and His-affinity purification is separate from the 2009 ASKA preparation. [PMID:31871051]

The 2020 E. coli PfkA comparison at 55 °C reports F6P apparent Km 0.065 mM/kcat 1.2 s−1 versus S7P 2.5 mM/0.25 s−1. Tabulated S7P efficiency0.15×10^3 differs from arithmetic using the rounded values and is not replaced. The coupled assay includes Mg 5 mM, ATP 2 mM, ADP 0.25 mM, rabbit aldolase4 U/ml, G3PDH2 U/ml and NADH0.15 mM. S7P was supplied as a Ba salt; this reagent form is retained as assay context, not a new core species. No TPI was added; trace TPI is a suggested explanation for unequal downstream peaks, not a new E. coli core participant. The separately cited2020 thesis DOI10.18174/510683 chapter6 supplement is not asserted byte-identical to the inaccessible journal supplement. PDF137 FigureS1 is a no-enzyme control; PDF140 FigureS4 shows both Michaelis–Menten S7P Km 2.489181822 mM and Hill K1/2=1.24179394 mM, n=1.603138135. Raw Vmax in dAbs/min is not kcat, and the fit comparison does not establish physiological bypass cooperativity. [DOI:10.18174/510683; PMID:31871051]

The clostridial PPi-dependent six-event MetaCycPWY-8178 definition is a separate pathway. Added rabbit aldolase in the 2020 coupling assay does not characterize a particular native clostridial aldolase. C. thermosuccinogenes ATP/GTP-PFK CDQ83_07225 showed no S7P activity up to 4 mM; its F6P ammonium dependence, very high Hill coefficient and proposed relief-valve role concern another enzyme and remain a hypothesis. The later engineered-clostridial LL1660 result (PMID36286488) removes both PPi-pfk and introduced TAL, limiting claims of universal necessity; the alternative C6↔C5 route remains unresolved. That result does not refute the E. coli ATP bypass assays. [MetaCyc:PWY-8178; MetaCyc:RXN-21730; PMID:31871051; PMID:36286488]

PfkA annotation supports Mg dependence, homotetramer and cytoplasmic location. Canonical F6P-dependent activity is inhibited by PEP and activated by ADP/GDP; F6P has a cooperative substrate response whereas ATP does not in the cited native context. These signs, the >90% contribution to wild-type canonical PFK activity, pH effects and in-vitro reverse activity are not direct measurements of S7P regulation or whole-pathway flux. S7P turnover and F6P turnover are separate substrate contexts. FbaA is a cytosolic class-II metal-dependent dimer. Native location/GO annotation is independent of SUBUNIT text. Two Zn sites per subunit (catalytic and structural) in the current annotation differ from the older PMID8436219 abstract's two Zn per dimer. The 2011 study (PMID22014167;2012 issue) separates untagged MG1655/pLEM1/pWKS30 material≥70% pure from pLEM5/pET28b His 6 WT and site mutants≥95% pure. As-purified metal content was up to 0.3 Zn/0.2 Ni per monomer; denaturation-assisted Zn loading produced2.3 Zn per monomer and 3.8-fold higher activity. Source numbering follows removed initiating methionine: His 110/226/264 catalytic ligands and Asp144/Glu174/Glu181 secondary-site ligands; historical His 108/111 is not silently renumbered. Native Co/Fe/Mn active metalloprotein alternatives are distinct from additive metal effects. Ni inhibits, Cu2+ strongly inhibits in vitro, low Zn slightly activates/high Zn slightly inhibits, Co slightly activates, and Ca/Mg/Mn had no effect in the measured preparation. Cytoplasmic copper is mainly cuprous, limiting physiological Cu2+ claims. Native K/ammonium activation cites personal communication in 1996; Ni/EDTA effects and earlier Crookes preparations remain source qualified. [EcoCyc:F16ALDOLASE-ENZRXN-CLASSII; EcoCyc:FRUCBISALD-CLASSII; EcoCyc:FRUCTBISALD-CLASSII-MONOMER; EcoCyc:REG0-12167; EcoCyc:REG0-12168; EcoCyc:REG0-12169; EcoCyc:REG0-8470; PMID:22014167; PMID:6996735; PMID:8436219; UniProtKB:P0AB71]

In PMID22014167, untagged FbaA 20 nM challenged with Ni 16 µM is protected by His 100 µM (about 20% loss instead of 70%); GSH 1 mM enhances Ni inhibition. These are conditional activity effects relative to Ni-only challenge, not generic ligand activation/inhibition or direct FbaA binding. The rcnA/gshA comparisons and D 144A/E174A resistance support contributions of cellular ligands and the secondary metal site without uniquely proving a Ni-delivery mechanism. Source-native His/GSH formula, charge and InChI ground selected reference chemical identities, while the assay ionic form remains unstated; inconsistent native CML SMILES is retained as a conflict. MG1655 growth inhibition at 8 µM Ni depends on carbon source (glucose/fructose versus glycerol/lactate/succinate), is bacteriostatic, and FbaA activity recovers after Ni removal even with translation inhibited. Active versus passive repair remains unresolved. [PMID:22014167]

UniProt FUNCTION text names GAP+E4P for SBP cleavage whereas its structured reaction and the 2009 direct assay support DHAP+E4P. Abstract-level PMID7872790 supports carbonyl substrate forms, Zn-dependent enediol(ate)-DHAP chemistry and pH effects; Cd replacement structures (PMID12595741) do not prove a physiological Cd cofactor or inhibition. Earlier phosphate-associated labeling (PMID3281666) and the later +76-Da mercaptoethanol adduct at source Cys36 (PMID7851430) concern different preparations; the latter ruled out phosphorylation and found no significant activity effect. Later phosphoproteome annotation (PMID35636362) does not reconcile these as a single constitutively modified active chain. Synthetic N-sulfonyl hydroxamate phosphate inhibitors and weaker phosphonate isosteres (PMID16236509) are bounded canonical-FBP context without an invented exact inhibitor identity. PMID31464375 uses His-tagged ASKA proteins (>90% purity;0.1 mM IPTG, 16 h at 37 °C, TALON purification). The 2019 NMR assay (15 µM monomer equivalent, 200 µM metabolites, 298 K; RF threshold0.1805/FPR5%) lists eleven FbaA binders:3PG, 6PG, AMP, ATP, citrate, GTP, malonate, NADP, PEP, PRPP and phenylpyruvate; six PfkA binders are AMP, CTP, FAD, FBP, GTP and NAD. These observations have no assigned causal sign merely from binding. The 2016 NMR paper PMID27065204 remains abstract/native scope; different buffers and thresholds limit direct comparison of binder sets. [PMID:27065204; PMID:31464375]

The 2019 direct FbaA assay uses canonical FBP 1 mM, Tris10 mM pH7.5/Mg 1 mM at 30 °C,≈1 µM enzyme monomer equivalent, modifiers5 mM (hypoxanthine3.22 mM), triplicate activities and quadruplicate mixture-specific MS calibration. ATP, 3PG and PEP activate; hypoxanthine and IMP have no effect. MS combines same-mass DHAP/GAP signals. ATP is within the cited physiological range, whereas 3PG/PEP are above it. The source reports prior3PG inhibition, while the 1995 abstract PMID7872790 reports no effect from glycolytic intermediates/ATP. These source/assay-specific outcomes remain separate, and the appendix's generic inhibitor caption does not reverse measured activation. None directly measures SBP cleavage regulation. [PMID:31464375; PMID:7872790]

Cra/FruR native PC00061 is a tetramer; the 1994 pT7-5 six-His assembly/ace-operator preparation (PMID8195118) differs from 1996 six-His binding-site/pfkA work (PMID8858581). Native pfkA regulatory records share siteBS785, and epd promoter records share BS264; epd-pgk-fbaA operon membership carries the fbaA expression interpretation. Cra-CPLX127 includes a native beta-D-fructofuranose1P component without a supplied ligand coefficient. Generic F1P assay identity is not assigned the native beta anomer. The 2018 abstract PMID29923648 reports F1P-dependent impairment of Cra DNA binding and negative FBP binding/effect tests, contrasting older FBP-effector discussion and the contaminant explanation in PMID30019355. Full2018 methods were unavailable. The 2021 Cra Asn50 cleavage/NTD behavior (PMID34666048) is a later preparation context, not proof that earlier specimens were cleaved. PMID19838295 compares JM101-derived PB11/PB12 ΔptsH ptsI crr backgrounds and rpoS derivatives under aerobic M9 glucose conditions, distinct from BW25113 talAB. Its pET28b+/ER2566 His-RpoS or His-RpoD combined with commercial RNAP core at core:sigma1:5 supports direct transcription of the first pfkA promoter. A sigma chain is not an autonomous polymerase. fbaA expression is condition-specific and can be operon-mediated; no immediate fbaA promoter was found in the tested analysis, which is not general promoter absence. Original MG1665 and pykA/pfkA-label discrepancies remain source errors rather than reference-strain reassignments. PMID16102000 abstract describes epd-pgk-fbaA cotranscription, RNaseE cleavage and segment stability without a uniquely determined signed RNaseE effect on FbaA catalysis. [PMID:16102000; PMID:19838295]

The csrA51 hypomorph in M9 glucose has reduced PfkA expression and partial growth/stress rescue after PfkA restoration (PMID26833659 plus native annotation). This is positive expression context, not a clean csrA deletion or a mapped direct RNA-binding site. Acid-associated pfkA response under aerobic but not microaerobic conditions is retained at abstract/native scope (PMID23274360), without assigning an unmeasured PhoB binding mechanism. [EcoCyc:6PFK-1-CPX; EcoCyc:TU0-45239; Entrez:947176; PMID:23274360; PMID:26833659]

PMID21272324 uses BW25113 Keio cyoA(JW0422), cydB(JW0723), fnr(sourceJW1318) and fur(JW0669) deletions in continuous aerobic culture (D 0.2 h−1, 37 °C, pH7, DO35–40%; C/N 1.68 or8.42). RT-PCR, with source controls, reports increased pfkA expression in the relevant deletion comparisons, amid broad network changes. Negative reference-associated effects are therefore qualified indirect knockout inferences, not direct pfkA binding. The source Fnr gene contrast under oxygen does not identify a purified anaerobic [4Fe-4S] active species, and CyoA/CydB reference chains do not autonomously reproduce their respiratory complexes. Exact subject-reference genes and the pfkA object gene are separately grounded. [Entrez:945295; Entrez:945651; Entrez:945908; PMID:21272324; UniProtKB:P0ABJ1; UniProtKB:P0ABK2]

Frozen PathBank memberPW002098.owl/rootSMP0002110 attaches Pentose PhosphateSMP0121065 (S7P-input/E4P-output context) and Glycolysis and Pyruvate DehydrogenaseSMP0000807 (DHAP-output context). Exact local compounds remain separate from Rhea: neutral S7P/E4P and a DHAP dilithium salt C3H5Li2O6P are not merged into anions. [PathBank:SMP0002110]

The Calvin-cycle and riboneogenesis condensation E4P+DHAP->SBP and subsequent SBP hydrolysis have different direction and energy chemistry. Classical PPP transaldolase uses S7P+GAP, while ADP-heptose formation isomerizes S7P. The ATP-dependent phosphorylation/cleavage pair is distinct from those routes and from the six-event PPi branch; shared metabolites and earlier research mentions do not merge the pathway definitions.

Native PfkA sequence-based NAD-kinase prediction, antisense/production engineering, altered carbon-catabolite repression and enzyme allostery studies are neighboring enzyme contexts, not additional bypass reactions. FbaA ts8/h8, RNA/engineered substrate variants and broader physiological annotations likewise do not demonstrate more steps in this pathway. Physical substrate channeling discussed speculatively in older work is not a demonstrated multienzyme complex. Older unavailable primary bodies remain explicitly abstract/native-annotation evidence. [EcoCyc:6PFK-1-CPX; EcoCyc:FRUCBISALD-CLASSII; PMID:7872790]

Physical substrate channeling discussed speculatively in older work is not a demonstrated multienzyme complex. Older unavailable primary bodies remain explicitly abstract/native-annotation evidence. [EcoCyc:6PFK-1-CPX; EcoCyc:FRUCBISALD-CLASSII; PMID:7872790]

The Calvin-cycle and riboneogenesis condensation E4P+DHAP->SBP and subsequent SBP hydrolysis have different direction and energy chemistry. Classical PPP transaldolase uses S7P+GAP, while ADP-heptose formation isomerizes S7P. The ATP-dependent phosphorylation/cleavage pair is distinct from those routes and from the six-event PPi branch; shared metabolites and earlier research mentions do not merge the pathway definitions.

Native PfkA sequence-based NAD-kinase prediction, antisense/production engineering, altered carbon-catabolite repression and enzyme allostery studies are neighboring enzyme contexts, not additional bypass reactions. FbaA ts8/h8, RNA/engineered substrate variants and broader physiological annotations likewise do not demonstrate more steps in this pathway. Physical substrate channeling discussed speculatively in older work is not a demonstrated multienzyme complex. Older unavailable primary bodies remain explicitly abstract/native-annotation evidence. [EcoCyc:6PFK-1-CPX; EcoCyc:FRUCBISALD-CLASSII; PMID:7872790]

This ATP-dependent two-event bypass converts sedoheptulose7-phosphate (S7P) through sedoheptulose1, 7-bisphosphate (SBP) to erythrose4-phosphate (E4P) and glycerone phosphate (DHAP). Exact Rhea chemistry is S7P + ATP -> SBP + ADP + H(+), followed by SBP -> E4P + DHAP. Native RXN0-6541 and SEDOBISALDOL-RXN map to directional RHEA31444 and cleavage30169; native 30170 is bidirectional and 30168 is condensation. The generic S7P class is distinct from alpha-pyranose CPD-19339/CHEBI133984. PfkA is a native homotetramer and FbaA a homodimer, not the mixed PfkA/PfkB assembly suggested by the frozen PathBank component list. Reference P0A796/b3916 and P0AB71/b2925 and MG1655 GeneIDs948412/947415 anchor identity; off-taxon GeneIDs93777982/93779073 belong to Shigella sonnei and are rejected. Database taxonomic range and reference identity do not establish unmodified wild-type flux in every strain. Two Zn sites per subunit (catalytic and structural) in the current annotation differ from the older PMID8436219 abstract's two Zn per dimer. The 2011 study (PMID22014167;2012 issue) separates untagged MG1655/pLEM1/pWKS30 material≥70% pure from pLEM5/pET28b His 6 WT and site mutants≥95% pure. As-purified metal content was up to 0.3 Zn/0.2 Ni per monomer; denaturation-assisted Zn loading produced2.3 Zn per monomer and 3.8-fold higher activity. Source numbering follows removed initiating methionine: His 110/226/264 catalytic ligands and Asp144/Glu174/Glu181 secondary-site ligands; historical His 108/111 is not silently renumbered. Native Co/Fe/Mn active metalloprotein alternatives are distinct from additive metal effects. Ni inhibits, Cu2+ strongly inhibits in vitro, low Zn slightly activates/high Zn slightly inhibits, Co slightly activates, and Ca/Mg/Mn had no effect in the measured preparation. Cytoplasmic copper is mainly cuprous, limiting physiological Cu2+ claims. Native K/ammonium activation cites personal communication in 1996; Ni/EDTA effects and earlier Crookes preparations remain source qualified. In PMID22014167, untagged FbaA 20 nM challenged with Ni 16 µM is protected by His 100 µM (about 20% loss instead of 70%); GSH 1 mM enhances Ni inhibition. These are conditional activity effects relative to Ni-only challenge, not generic ligand activation/inhibition or direct FbaA binding. The rcnA/gshA comparisons and D 144A/E174A resistance support contributions of cellular ligands and the secondary metal site without uniquely proving a Ni-delivery mechanism. Source-native His/GSH formula, charge and InChI ground selected reference chemical identities, while the assay ionic form remains unstated; inconsistent native CML SMILES is retained as a conflict. MG1655 growth inhibition at 8 µM Ni depends on carbon source (glucose/fructose versus glycerol/lactate/succinate), is bacteriostatic, and FbaA activity recovers after Ni removal even with translation inhibited. Active versus passive repair remains unresolved. [PMID:22014167]

The later engineered-clostridial LL1660 result (PMID36286488) removes both PPi-pfk and introduced TAL, limiting claims of universal necessity; the alternative C6↔C5 route remains unresolved. That result does not refute the E. coli ATP bypass assays. [MetaCyc:PWY-8178; MetaCyc:RXN-21730; PMID:31871051; PMID:36286488]

PfkA annotation supports Mg dependence, homotetramer and cytoplasmic location. Canonical F6P-dependent activity is inhibited by PEP and activated by ADP/GDP; F6P has a cooperative substrate response whereas ATP does not in the cited native context. These signs, the >90% contribution to wild-type canonical PFK activity, pH effects and in-vitro reverse activity are not direct measurements of S7P regulation or whole-pathway flux. S7P turnover and F6P turnover are separate substrate contexts. [EcoCyc:6PFK-1-CPX; EcoCyc:6PFRUCTPHOS-ENZRXN; EcoCyc:REG0-7473; EcoCyc:REG0-7474; EcoCyc:REG0-7475; EcoCyc:REG0-7476; UniProtKB:P0A796]

FbaA is a cytosolic class-II metal-dependent dimer. Native location/GO annotation is independent of SUBUNIT text. Two Zn sites per subunit (catalytic and structural) in the current annotation differ from the older PMID8436219 abstract's two Zn per dimer. The 2011 study (PMID22014167;2012 issue) separates untagged MG1655/pLEM1/pWKS30 material≥70% pure from pLEM5/pET28b His 6 WT and site mutants≥95% pure. As-purified metal content was up to 0.3 Zn/0.2 Ni per monomer; denaturation-assisted Zn loading produced2.3 Zn per monomer and 3.8-fold higher activity. Source numbering follows removed initiating methionine: His 110/226/264 catalytic ligands and Asp144/Glu174/Glu181 secondary-site ligands; historical His 108/111 is not silently renumbered. Native Co/Fe/Mn active metalloprotein alternatives are distinct from additive metal effects. Ni inhibits, Cu2+ strongly inhibits in vitro, low Zn slightly activates/high Zn slightly inhibits, Co slightly activates, and Ca/Mg/Mn had no effect in the measured preparation. Cytoplasmic copper is mainly cuprous, limiting physiological Cu2+ claims. Native K/ammonium activation cites personal communication in 1996; Ni/EDTA effects and earlier Crookes preparations remain source qualified. [EcoCyc:F16ALDOLASE-ENZRXN-CLASSII; EcoCyc:FRUCBISALD-CLASSII; EcoCyc:FRUCTBISALD-CLASSII-MONOMER; EcoCyc:REG0-12167; EcoCyc:REG0-12168; EcoCyc:REG0-12169; EcoCyc:REG0-8470; PMID:22014167; PMID:6996735; PMID:8436219; UniProtKB:P0AB71]

In PMID22014167, untagged FbaA 20 nM challenged with Ni 16 µM is protected by His 100 µM (about 20% loss instead of 70%); GSH 1 mM enhances Ni inhibition. These are conditional activity effects relative to Ni-only challenge, not generic ligand activation/inhibition or direct FbaA binding. The rcnA/gshA comparisons and D 144A/E174A resistance support contributions of cellular ligands and the secondary metal site without uniquely proving a Ni-delivery mechanism. Source-native His/GSH formula, charge and InChI ground selected reference chemical identities, while the assay ionic form remains unstated; inconsistent native CML SMILES is retained as a conflict. MG1655 growth inhibition at 8 µM Ni depends on carbon source (glucose/fructose versus glycerol/lactate/succinate), is bacteriostatic, and FbaA activity recovers after Ni removal even with translation inhibited. Active versus passive repair remains unresolved. [PMID:22014167]

UniProt FUNCTION text names GAP+E4P for SBP cleavage whereas its structured reaction and the 2009 direct assay support DHAP+E4P. Abstract-level PMID7872790 supports carbonyl substrate forms, Zn-dependent enediol(ate)-DHAP chemistry and pH effects; Cd replacement structures (PMID12595741) do not prove a physiological Cd cofactor or inhibition. Earlier phosphate-associated labeling (PMID3281666) and the later +76-Da mercaptoethanol adduct at source Cys36 (PMID7851430) concern different preparations; the latter ruled out phosphorylation and found no significant activity effect. Later phosphoproteome annotation (PMID35636362) does not reconcile these as a single constitutively modified active chain. Synthetic N-sulfonyl hydroxamate phosphate inhibitors and weaker phosphonate isosteres (PMID16236509) are bounded canonical-FBP context without an invented exact inhibitor identity. [EcoCyc:FRUCBISALD-CLASSII; PMID:12595741; PMID:16236509; PMID:19756045; PMID:3281666; PMID:35636362; PMID:7851430; PMID:7872790; UniProtKB:P0AB71]

PMID31464375 uses His-tagged ASKA proteins (>90% purity;0.1 mM IPTG, 16 h at 37 °C, TALON purification). The 2019 NMR assay (15 µM monomer equivalent, 200 µM metabolites, 298 K; RF threshold0.1805/FPR5%) lists eleven FbaA binders:3PG, 6PG, AMP, ATP, citrate, GTP, malonate, NADP, PEP, PRPP and phenylpyruvate; six PfkA binders are AMP, CTP, FAD, FBP, GTP and NAD. These observations have no assigned causal sign merely from binding. The 2016 NMR paper PMID27065204 remains abstract/native scope; different buffers and thresholds limit direct comparison of binder sets. [PMID:27065204; PMID:31464375]

The 2019 direct FbaA assay uses canonical FBP 1 mM, Tris10 mM pH7.5/Mg 1 mM at 30 °C,≈1 µM enzyme monomer equivalent, modifiers5 mM (hypoxanthine3.22 mM), triplicate activities and quadruplicate mixture-specific MS calibration. ATP, 3PG and PEP activate; hypoxanthine and IMP have no effect. MS combines same-mass DHAP/GAP signals. ATP is within the cited physiological range, whereas 3PG/PEP are above it. The source reports prior3PG inhibition, while the 1995 abstract PMID7872790 reports no effect from glycolytic intermediates/ATP. These source/assay-specific outcomes remain separate, and the appendix's generic inhibitor caption does not reverse measured activation. None directly measures SBP cleavage regulation. [PMID:31464375; PMID:7872790]

Cra/FruR native PC00061 is a tetramer; the 1994 pT7-5 six-His assembly/ace-operator preparation (PMID8195118) differs from 1996 six-His binding-site/pfkA work (PMID8858581). Native pfkA regulatory records share siteBS785, and epd promoter records share BS264; epd-pgk-fbaA operon membership carries the fbaA expression interpretation. Cra-CPLX127 includes a native beta-D-fructofuranose1P component without a supplied ligand coefficient. Generic F1P assay identity is not assigned the native beta anomer. The 2018 abstract PMID29923648 reports F1P-dependent impairment of Cra DNA binding and negative FBP binding/effect tests, contrasting older FBP-effector discussion and the contaminant explanation in PMID30019355. Full2018 methods were unavailable. The 2021 Cra Asn50 cleavage/NTD behavior (PMID34666048) is a later preparation context, not proof that earlier specimens were cleaved. [EcoCyc:CPLX-127; EcoCyc:D-fructofuranose-1-phosphate; EcoCyc:FRU1P; EcoCyc:PC00061; EcoCyc:PD00521; EcoCyc:REG0-15081; EcoCyc:REG0-15233; EcoCyc:REG0-4838; EcoCyc:REG0-5630; PMID:19838295; PMID:29923648; PMID:30019355; PMID:34666048; PMID:8195118; PMID:8577250; PMID:8858581]

Native CRP-cAMP CPLX0-226 contains CRP dimerPC00004 and cAMP; PC00004 has two P0ACJ8 chains, but ligand stoichiometry is not supplied. Positive epd-pgk-fbaA regulation is limited by the 1998 PMID9851989 abstract: deleting the CRP site had little effect under glucose whereas crp/cya loss strongly reduced epd/gapB P0, supporting an indirect response. PtsG-encoded IICBGlc contributes to glucose stimulation of that promoter. It is distinct from crr/EIIAGlc, does not establish a direct fbaA operator and is not a pathway-specific S7P transporter. [EcoCyc:CAMP; EcoCyc:CPLX0-226; EcoCyc:PC00004; EcoCyc:PD00257; EcoCyc:REG0-15234; EcoCyc:REG0-5629; Entrez:945295; Entrez:945651; PMID:9851989; UniProtKB:P0A9A9; UniProtKB:P0A9E5; UniProtKB:P13445; UniProtKB:P69783; UniProtKB:P69786; UniProtKB:P69913]

PMID19838295 compares JM101-derived PB11/PB12 ΔptsH ptsI crr backgrounds and rpoS derivatives under aerobic M9 glucose conditions, distinct from BW25113 talAB. Its pET28b+/ER2566 His-RpoS or His-RpoD combined with commercial RNAP core at core:sigma1:5 supports direct transcription of the first pfkA promoter. A sigma chain is not an autonomous polymerase. fbaA expression is condition-specific and can be operon-mediated; no immediate fbaA promoter was found in the tested analysis, which is not general promoter absence. Original MG1665 and pykA/pfkA-label discrepancies remain source errors rather than reference-strain reassignments. PMID16102000 abstract describes epd-pgk-fbaA cotranscription, RNaseE cleavage and segment stability without a uniquely determined signed RNaseE effect on FbaA catalysis. [PMID:16102000; PMID:19838295]

The csrA51 hypomorph in M9 glucose has reduced PfkA expression and partial growth/stress rescue after PfkA restoration (PMID26833659 plus native annotation). This is positive expression context, not a clean csrA deletion or a mapped direct RNA-binding site. Acid-associated pfkA response under aerobic but not microaerobic conditions is retained at abstract/native scope (PMID23274360), without assigning an unmeasured PhoB binding mechanism. [EcoCyc:6PFK-1-CPX; EcoCyc:TU0-45239; Entrez:947176; PMID:23274360; PMID:26833659]

PMID21272324 uses BW25113 Keio cyoA(JW0422), cydB(JW0723), fnr(sourceJW1318) and fur(JW0669) deletions in continuous aerobic culture (D 0.2 h−1, 37 °C, pH7, DO35–40%; C/N 1.68 or8.42). RT-PCR, with source controls, reports increased pfkA expression in the relevant deletion comparisons, amid broad network changes. Negative reference-associated effects are therefore qualified indirect knockout inferences, not direct pfkA binding. The source Fnr gene contrast under oxygen does not identify a purified anaerobic [4Fe-4S] active species, and CyoA/CydB reference chains do not autonomously reproduce their respiratory complexes. Exact subject-reference genes and the pfkA object gene are separately grounded. [Entrez:945295; Entrez:945651; Entrez:945908; PMID:21272324; UniProtKB:P0ABJ1; UniProtKB:P0ABK2]

Frozen PathBank memberPW002098.owl/rootSMP0002110 attaches Pentose PhosphateSMP0121065 (S7P-input/E4P-output context) and Glycolysis and Pyruvate DehydrogenaseSMP0000807 (DHAP-output context). Their generic Interaction markers are unsigned structural membership, not transport or inhibition. Exact local compounds remain separate from Rhea: neutral S7P/E4P and a DHAP dilithium salt C3H5Li2O6P are not merged into anions. The frozen neutral ATP/ADP/SBP forms and erroneous PfkB inclusion are explicit source conflicts. The original wholeZIP/member/root provenance is retained, with no live per-pathway download claim. [PathBank:SMP0002110]

The Calvin-cycle and riboneogenesis condensation E4P+DHAP->SBP and subsequent SBP hydrolysis have different direction and energy chemistry. Classical PPP transaldolase uses S7P+GAP, while ADP-heptose formation isomerizes S7P. The ATP-dependent phosphorylation/cleavage pair is distinct from those routes and from the six-event PPi branch; shared metabolites and earlier research mentions do not merge the pathway definitions.

Native PfkA sequence-based NAD-kinase prediction, antisense/production engineering, altered carbon-catabolite repression and enzyme allostery studies are neighboring enzyme contexts, not additional bypass reactions. FbaA ts8/h8, RNA/engineered substrate variants and broader physiological annotations likewise do not demonstrate more steps in this pathway. Physical substrate channeling discussed speculatively in older work is not a demonstrated multienzyme complex. Older unavailable primary bodies remain explicitly abstract/native-annotation evidence. [EcoCyc:6PFK-1-CPX; EcoCyc:FRUCBISALD-CLASSII; PMID:7872790]

Single-turnover THI13 chemistry inferred by similarity to THI5 (ECO:0000250, UniProtKB:P43534). Histidine and PLP-lysine are protein-bound residues, not free histidine substrates. HMP-phosphate is the product. The inherited exact iron redox, water/proton balance, 3-oxopropanoate and residue-product assertions are quarantined: PMID:35675507 reports Fe(II)/oxygen dependence and different PLP-derived products for Candida albicans THI5, and a histidine-derived alpha-ketoacid for both Candida THI5 and S. cerevisiae THI5. These homolog experiments are not direct evidence for S. cerevisiae THI13; no replacement oxygen or product edges, or complete net stoichiometry, are inferred. Omitted products and balancing species remain unresolved, rather than asserted absent.
